initial_requirements: USDA Agricultural Research Service needs a centralized system for watershed research data that is currently managed separately at individual sites. Watershed staff should upload and maintain standardized water, soil, land-management, conservation, and economic data, while researchers and approved public users can search, analyze, visualize, download, and report integrated datasets. Access must reflect the responsibilities and confidentiality limits of different user groups.

slots.key: Data quality, retention, and versioning controls
slots.value: The repository should include controls for data quality, retention, and versioning so it preserves the history of what came from each site and when, and it should fail gracefully to protect data already in the system if a load goes wrong or a site outage occurs. If a load fails partway through, the repository should not publish the partial set as the active version; already ingested records can be kept in a staging or failed-run area for review, while the last known good version remains visible until the whole run is successfully completed and validated. Staff should be able to rerun the same load after fixing the problem, and rollback should restore the previous approved version rather than trying to stitch together a mixed state.

slots.key: Mandatory validation rules for standardized dataset submission
slots.value: Common definitions are needed for site, watershed, treatment, plot, observation period, water, soil, land management, conservation practice, and economic data; shared meaning is also needed for units, measurement methods, location references, and coding of conditions or events so data can be compared, combined, and reliably reported across sites. A little variation is acceptable if it is limited to site-specific details that do not break the shared structure, such as local naming conventions or extra context fields. Differences that affect core variables, units, date formats, or required metadata must be remapped or corrected to fit the common standard, and sites should not invent their own schema versions. The repository should normalize to the approved common vocabulary, units, and date/time conventions first, preserve the original site value in a separate source field, use a maintained crosswalk table to map local codes or terms to standard terms, flag anything that cannot be mapped cleanly for review, and convert measurements to the standard unit while recording the conversion used.

slots.key: Data quality, retention, and versioning controls
slots.value: The repository should include controls for data quality, retention, and versioning so it preserves the history of what came from each site and when; readiness for release depends on completion of cleanup, quality checks, and metadata. Issues affecting the meaning, quality, or privacy of the dataset must be corrected before release rather than waived. If a load fails partway through, the repository should not publish the partial set as the active version. Already ingested records may be kept in a staging or failed-run area for review, while the last known good version remains visible until the whole run is successfully completed and validated. For retries, staff should be able to rerun the same load after fixing the problem, and rollback should restore the previous approved version rather than creating a mixed state. Anything that breaks dataset integrity should block publication, including missing required metadata, invalid units or dates, duplicate records that can’t be resolved, failed access-rule assignment, and values that don’t pass basic range and format checks. If the system can’t confidently verify the dataset against its required rules, it should stop the run rather than risk publishing questionable data.

slots.value: Site-managed data currently starts in the field with manual collection or instrument output, then is cleaned and organized locally by site staff before being loaded into site-specific systems or files. In practice, much of the cleaned data is still kept in local databases, spreadsheets, shared drives, or a mix of those, with no common repository or common maintenance approach across sites.

slots.key: Data conversion, cleansing, and deduplication needs
slots.value: Data is cleaned and organized locally before loading; pulling everything together centrally takes extra effort because formats, naming, and timing are inconsistent across sites. The repository should normalize to the approved common vocabulary, units, and date/time conventions first, keep the original site value in a separate source field, use a maintained crosswalk table to map local terms to standard terms, flag anything that cannot be mapped cleanly for review, and convert measurements to the standard unit while recording the conversion used so comparisons across sites and years stay consistent without rebuilding the whole dataset.

topics.topic_content: Release planning and operational rollout across watershed sites

slots.key: Phased release approach and site onboarding sequence
slots.value: A site first confirms its data is organized, validated, and mapped to the standard structure, then it is reviewed by the responsible staff or steward before being opened up more broadly.

slots.key: Training and support needed for staff adoption
slots.value: Initial training on the standardized data model, validation rules, confidentiality and release process, plus hands-on onboarding for the upload and review workflow; ongoing refresher training, written guidance, access to someone who can answer questions about unusual data issues, and periodic quality checks or feedback to catch mistakes early.

topics.topic_content: Requirement priorities, acceptance criteria, and open issues

slots.key: Highest-priority capabilities for first delivery
slots.value: Stay usable as data volume and variety grow so staff can still search, load, and download data without long delays or a lot of manual cleanup; handle differences across sites and years without breaking comparison or forcing staff to rework everything for each new dataset; support researchers and approved users in finding integrated data quickly and knowing what is complete, current, and appropriate to use.

slots.key: Acceptance criteria for key workflows and access rules
slots.value: When staff encounter an unusual data issue during rollout, they should first log the issue and route it to the site steward or designated reviewer, then to the central data governance contact if it affects the standard or confidentiality rules. Minor, well-documented issues may be allowed as temporary exceptions, but only if they do not alter the scientific interpretation, do not create a confidentiality risk, and do not violate any required field or validation rule considered mandatory. The note must state what the issue was, which records or fields were affected, what workaround or correction was applied, what remains unresolved, and who approved the exception. Issues affecting the meaning, quality, or privacy of the dataset must be corrected before release rather than waived.

slots.key: Known risks, dependencies, and unresolved decisions
slots.value: Unresolved decisions include how strict validation needs to be, what counts as a recoverable failure, and whether some sites need exceptions for local workflows or offline uploads. Dependencies still need confirmation on identity management, storage, and the rules governing approved public versus internal access, since these affect whether a run can be published or must stay staged. Before normal use, business rules should require a load to be either fully approved or not published at all, with any exceptions explicit, documented, and reviewed rather than handled ad hoc.
